summary: Added write_chart_edits<W: Write + ?Sized> and WritePatchError. Both APIs reuse the existing planner and shared pre-output span validation; streaming writes borrowed unchanged XML slices and owned planned fragments without building the whole output. Added six integration tests.

commands.outcome: Passed; formatted implementation and new tests.

Initial run failed: 165 existing tests passed; 5 of 6 integration tests passed. The payload identity test constructed an io::Error containing Box<Payload>, then incorrectly attempted to downcast directly to Payload. Corrected the test setup by coercing the box to Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync> before constructing io::Error.
Passed after correcting the test setup.
Passed: 165 existing unit tests, 6 new integration tests; 0 doctests.

design_decisions: The caller retains ownership of xml, ChartData, edits and writer. The writer bound accepts unsized trait objects. Only replacement bytes and structural fragments are owned by the planner.

A shared planning helper runs add and finish for both output APIs. A shared validation helper checks every bound before sorting, then every overlap before output starts; it retains the previous sorting and error precedence.
The streaming path uses write_all for each borrowed original slice and planned replacement. This preserves short-write, Interrupted and WriteZero handling and never flushes or closes the writer.

WritePatchError owns either the unchanged PatchError or original io::Error. Display adds context; Error::source exposes the original typed cause. PatchError gained an additive Error implementation without changing variants, public structs or prior function signatures.

Invalid template ranges now use checked slice access; empty templates and inconsistent clone metadata return existing errors rather than arithmetic/indexing panics. Existing inline tests were preserved.

Tests cover every edit variant, mixed point/series edits, insertion ordering, byte preservation, borrowed trait-object writers, late range and overlap validation, custom error payload identity, prefix failures, short writes, Interrupted, WriteZero and no flush.
limitations: I/O failure may leave an output prefix and offers no rollback. Validation failures leave the writer untouched.
This is an isolated component check with synthetic chart fixtures, not full document-engine or visual validation.
No allocation benchmark was run. The no-whole-output-buffer property is supported by inspection of the direct slice-writing path; structural replacement fragments still allocate as allowed.
